builderInsights.suggestedTitle: Google 的 AI 逆袭，本质上是一场系统战
builderInsights.suggestedSummary: 大家都说，Gemini 的崛起不是靠运气。真正起作用的，是把 model playbook、客户反馈闭环和 enterprise 业务一块搭起来，直到这些拼图在 Gemini 3 上彻底对上。这个复盘挺直接：Google 是怎么从落后 OpenAI 和 Anthropic，重新回到前沿的。还有一条：他们要离开 Google 了，而且那个 toddler 的 shoutout 也确实帮了不少忙。

tweets.text:
I'm moving on from @Google.

I had the privilege of helping build two businesses from zero: first across Search & Ads, then Gemini.

Three years ago, OpenAI and Anthropic were in the lead. We built what it took to compete: the playbook for building AI models, the customer feedback flywheel, and the enterprise business. Gemini 3 was the moment those systems came together.

To the Gemini team: we went from underdogs to competing at the frontier. Keep pushing.

For now, I'm enjoying the emergent capabilities of some real intelligence at home - my toddler. She's been quietly shipping.

builderInsights.authorBio: ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
builderInsights.title: Aaron Levie
builderInsights.suggestedTitle: AI 把容易的部分抹平了，差异化就会转移
builderInsights.suggestedSummary: 他的观点是：只要 AI 让某件事变简单，别人很快也能拿到同样的能力。所以真正的优势会转到别的地方。对 software 来说，这意味着 sales、marketing 和 customer success 会更重要；对 finance 来说，重点是 client engagement。核心问题很直接：如果大家都能做你能做的事，那到底是什么让你和别人不一样？

tweets.text:
When AI makes one thing easy to do, it’s always good to assume that will equally be the case for everyone else. If it’s the case for everyone else, then that means competitive forces will ensure that resources move to new or other areas that create differentiation.

If AI makes building software easier, then there will be a relative increase in resources going into sales, marketing, and customer success, because standing out or going deeper with customers else becomes even more important. 

This will also apply to lots of other areas of work. If you automate getting financial advice and insights, then the differentiation is in client engagement. And on and on.

Just ask yourself: if everyone else does exactly what I do with this technology, how will I stand out from everyone else? That’s what happens next.

podcastHighlights.source: The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck
podcastHighlights.title: OpenAI 董事会成员 Zico Kolter 谈前沿 AI 的真实风险
podcastHighlights.suggestedTitle: Zico Kolter 说，AI safety 不会只靠更大的 model 自然变好
podcastHighlights.suggestedSummary:
**核心结论：** 前沿 AI 只有把 safety 直接做进系统里，才会真正更安全。指望 scale 自己解决问题，不现实。

- 更大的 model 默认会提升能力，但 robustness、jailbreak resistance 和 misuse prevention 不会自己同步变好。
- AI risk 不是一个问题。错误、恶意使用、社会影响、失控风险，都需要不同的防线。
- governance 在实际中很重要；如果证据不够，OpenAI 的 safety committee 可以把 release 按住。

Zico Kolter 是 OpenAI board member，也是 Safety and Security Committee 的 chair。他看 AI safety 的角度很全：一边管 Carnegie Mellon 的 machine learning department，一边做了很多年 AI security research。他的核心判断很直接："You can’t just sort of trust models to get safer by getting bigger." 能力会飞快增长，但 safety 不会自动跟上。

所以他一直在推 layered defenses，而不是靠玄学。OpenAI 的 preparedness framework，Anthropic 和 Google 的类似系统，都会给 bio、cyber、self-improvement 这类高风险能力设门槛。但 Kolter 说，这只是问题的一部分。真正的 safety stack 还得覆盖 model behavior、user misuse，以及 AI 逐渐嵌进各个场景后的整个 ecosystem。

他尤其不看好那种“等下一个 model 就好了”的懒办法。做 math 或 coding 也许行。做 robustness 不行。正如他所说，"to make models more robust, to make them broadly safer, you need to be explicit in training them for safety." 说白了，safety 是设计出来的，不是顺带长出来的。

Kolter 也不认同那种漫画式的“doomer vs. accelerationist”叙事。他觉得，大多数认真研究的人其实站在同一边：看好 AI 的上限，也不愿意忽视它的下限。真正该问的，不是 AI 到底是好是坏，而是行业有没有把 governance、monitoring 和 release discipline 搭起来，跟上这些 system 现在已经能做的事。
